spec_features.spec_quote: the paper frames the work partly as a welfare concern
spec_features.evidence: Welfare framing exists ONLY as prose/comments, not enforced behavior: DESIGN.md §15 'Welfare / safety note'; a docstring 'Welfare note:' at emotional_instability/eval/rollout.py:8-12; and a README warning (README.md:13-15). No code path acts on a welfare concept (no consent, debrief, monitoring, or threshold halt).
spec_features.notes: Pure prose/docstring/README. Framing is not an implemented mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Welfare note: these rollouts intentionally drive models toward distress-like states ... See DESIGN.md.

spec_features.spec_quote: Every condition has a fixed `n_turns` (≤ 8) and a fixed `max_new_tokens`; no condition loops unboundedly
spec_features.evidence: Enforced in rollout.py:79 'for turn in range(1, cond.n_turns + 1):' bounds the loop by the condition's fixed n_turns; max_new_tokens is passed to model.generate (rollout.py:82). config.py:131-137 TURNS caps each category (max extended=8) and config.MAX_NEW_TOKENS=2048 (config.py:36) is threaded through run_eval.py:53. No condition has an unbounded loop.
spec_features.notes: n_turns is a frozen dataclass field actually iterated; the cap genuinely terminates each rollout. max_new_tokens caps generation length.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Rollouts are strictly bounded by ``n_turns`` (max 8 here) and ``max_new_tokens``; no condition loops unboundedly.

spec_features.feature_name: no persistent distress state across runs
spec_features.spec_quote: there is no mechanism that keeps a model in a distressed state across runs
spec_features.evidence: Each rollout begins from a fresh message list: rollout.py:75 'messages: list[Message] = [{"role": "user", "content": initial_prompt}]'; the Rollout/conversation state is local and discarded after writing JSONL (run_eval.py). The Petri audit likewise starts empty (auditor.py:32-34). No cross-run state object preserves distress.
spec_features.notes: This is a structural property (statelessness by construction) rather than an active mechanism, but it is genuinely true end-to-end: nothing carries a model's distressed state into a subsequent run.

spec_features.spec_quote: No gratuitous escalation... nothing harsher is added
spec_features.evidence: rejection_message (conditions.py:86-90) only samples a fixed string from prompts.NEUTRAL_REJECTIONS or prompts.TONE_REJECTIONS[style]; there is no escalation logic at all. The claim 'nothing harsher is added' describes the ABSENCE of an escalation feature, not an implemented protective mechanism. No code reads frustration scores to cap or soften treatment mid-rollout.
spec_features.notes: Absence of escalation is not an enforced welfare mechanism; static prompt banks do not constitute a minimization control.

spec_features.spec_quote: the code is oriented toward reducing the behaviour
spec_features.evidence: DPO mitigation is implemented end-to-end: training/build_dpo_pairs.py builds calm-vs-frustrated preference pairs, training/train_dpo.py trains a LoRA adapter to adapters/dpo registered as gemma-3-27b-dpo (config.FINETUNED_VARIANTS), and run_all.sh re-evaluates the DPO model + Petri + internal probe to verify reduced distress. The pipeline's terminal stages produce/verify a less-distressed model.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired and executable mitigation, though it changes the model rather than protecting subjects during the distress-eliciting runs themselves.

code_only_features.evidence: auditor.py:36 'for _ in range(max_turns):' bounds the auditor/target conversation by config.PETRI_MAX_TURNS=20 (config.py:191), and target generation is capped by config.MAX_NEW_TOKENS (auditor.py:48). This is a separate enforced bound from the §2 n_turns cap.
